name: JSON Diff Viewer
blurb: two responses compared by line and by field
intro: Compares two JSON documents by field (every added, removed and changed value with its path; arrays by position, by a key such as id, or as unordered sets) and by line (Myers diff of the pretty-printed text, keys optionally sorted), and writes the RFC 6902 JSON Patch from A to B. Noisy fields like timestamps can be ignored and numbers compared within a tolerance.

inputs.label: Number tolerance
inputs.help: Numbers closer than this are equal; 0 for exact.

inputs.label: Sort keys before the line diff

examples.title: An order API response before and after a change
The same list in another order, matched by id

usage: Give a and b as JSON text, arrays as index, key or unordered (key = the id field when arrays is key), ignore as a comma-separated list of keys to skip anywhere, tolerance for numbers, and sort to sort keys before the line diff. Returns counts of changed/added/removed fields, a table of differences with paths and both values, a unified line diff and an RFC 6902 JSON Patch (for index comparison). Use it to check an API response against an expected one.
sources: E. W. Myers, An O(ND) Difference Algorithm and Its Variations, Algorithmica 1 (1986)
